Frederikshavn is a Danish municipality evaluated in the 2022–2023 Annual Report from the Danish Atrial Fibrillation Database (AFDK), published by the Regions' Clinical Quality Development Programme (RKKP). The report assesses the clinical quality of atrial fibrillation treatment across Denmark, emphasizing the decentralized responsibility for healthcare quality development and benchmarking all 98 Danish municipalities.

In the context of Indicator 4b, which measures compliance with safety practices regarding the use and monitoring of DOAC (Direct Oral Anticoagulant) medications, Frederikshavn performed exceptionally well. The municipality met the required standard, achieving a compliance rate of 97.7% (1,404 out of 1,437 eligible patients) and was marked as "Yes" for fulfilling the indicator [^src1]. This places Frederikshavn among the highest-performing municipalities in this specific metric.

Additionally, Frederikshavn was evaluated on other key quality indicators detailed in the latter sections of the report, which focus on the early initiation of anticoagulation therapy and the prevention of ischemic strokes. For these metrics, the municipality again achieved a "Yes" status, recording figures of 6 out of 1,800 and 16 out of 1,797 in the respective statistical breakdowns [^src2]. While the data does not detail specific local interventions, Frederikshavn's consistent compliance highlights its role in the broader national framework for monitoring and improving cardiovascular care at the municipal level.
